\section{Monads}
\subsection{Monoids on the Category of Endofunctors}
For $[\mathcal{C},\mathcal{C}]$ the category of endofunctors, with
\begin{itemize}
    \item objects - functors 
    \[F:\mathcal{C} \times \mathcal{C}\]
    \item morphisms - natural transformations
    \[\phi: F\rightarrow G\]
\end{itemize}
Define 
\[F\otimes G := FG\]
\[I := 1_\mathcal{C}\]

\begin{note}
In what sense can I have a natural transformation in parallel?

Think of $G$ as some structure on the inside, and $F$ as structure on the outside.
Do some operation on $G$, also doing the same operation on $F$ in parallel
\end{note}

\subsection{Natural transformations "in parallel"}
\begin{example}
Define
\[\texttt{List} : \textbf{Set} \rightarrow \textbf{Set}\]
\[X \mapsto \texttt{List}\ X\]
where \texttt{List}$(X)$ is the set of finite lists and elements of $X$
\[f: X\rightarrow Y\]
\[\texttt{List}(f) : \texttt{List}\ X \rightarrow \texttt{List}\ Y\]
\[[x_1,...,x_k] \mapsto [f(x_1), ... , f(x_k)]\]

Define also
\[\texttt{BTree}: \textbf{Set} \rightarrow \textbf{Set}\]
\[X \mapsto \texttt{BTree}\ X\]
where \texttt{BTree}$(X)$ is the set of finite binary trees with leaves labelled by elements of $X$
% https://q.uiver.app/#
\[\left\{\begin{tikzcd}
	&& \bullet \\
	& \bullet && {x_3} \\
	{x_1} && {x_2}
	\arrow[no head, from=1-3, to=2-2]
	\arrow[no head, from=2-2, to=3-1]
	\arrow[no head, from=2-2, to=3-3]
	\arrow[no head, from=1-3, to=2-4]
\end{tikzcd}, ...\right\}\]

\[f: X\rightarrow Y\]
\[\texttt{BTree}(f) : \texttt{BTree}\ X \rightarrow \texttt{BTree}\ Y\]
% https://q.uiver.app/#
\[\begin{tikzcd}
	&& \bullet &&&&& \bullet \\
	& \bullet && {x_3} & {} & {} & \bullet && {f(x_3)} \\
	{x_1} && {x_2} &&& {f(x_1)} && {f(x_2)}
	\arrow[no head, from=1-3, to=2-2]
	\arrow[no head, from=2-2, to=3-1]
	\arrow[no head, from=2-2, to=3-3]
	\arrow[no head, from=1-3, to=2-4]
	\arrow[maps to, from=2-5, to=2-6]
	\arrow[no head, from=2-7, to=3-6]
	\arrow[no head, from=2-7, to=1-8]
	\arrow[no head, from=1-8, to=2-9]
	\arrow[no head, from=2-7, to=3-8]
\end{tikzcd}\]

\end{example}

\begin{theorem}[Informal]
    It is possible to apply natural transformations "over" or "under" functors. 
    
\end{theorem}
Let
\[\phi: F\rightarrow F'\]
\begin{definition}["Over"]
    \[\phi \otimes G : FG \rightarrow F' G\]
    \[(\phi \otimes G)_A := \phi_{G\ A} : FGA \rightarrow FG'A\]
    which is natural as it follows from the naturality of $\phi$
\end{definition}
\begin{definition}["Under"]
    \[G \otimes \phi : GF \rightarrow GF'\]
    \[(G\otimes \phi)_A := G(\phi_A) : GFA \rightarrow GF'A\]
\end{definition}

\begin{example}
\[\texttt{rev} : \texttt{List} \rightarrow \texttt{List}\]
\[\texttt{rev}_A ([a_1,...,a_k]) = [a_k,...,a_1]\]

	& {[a_k,...,a_1]} & {[f(a_k),...,f(a_1)]} \\
	{\texttt{List}\ A} &&& {\texttt{List}\ B}
	\arrow["{\texttt{rev}_A}", from=1-1, to=4-1]
	\arrow["{\texttt{List}(f)}", from=1-1, to=1-4]
	\arrow["{\texttt{rev}_B}", from=1-4, to=4-4]

	\arrow[maps to, from=2-2, to=3-2]
	\arrow[maps to, from=3-2, to=3-3]
	\arrow[maps to, from=2-3, to=3-3]
\end{tikzcd}\]

\[\texttt{rev} \otimes \texttt{BTree} : 
\texttt{List} \circ \texttt{BTree} \rightarrow \texttt{List}\circ \texttt{BTree}\]

\subsection{Results}

\begin{proposition}
    For natural transformations
    \[\phi: F\rightarrow F', \quad \psi: G \rightarrow G'\]
    we have
    \[(\phi\otimes G') \circ (F\otimes \psi) = (F' \otimes \psi) \circ (\phi \otimes G) =: \phi \otimes \psi\]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
\[(\phi \otimes G')_A \circ (F\otimes \psi)_A = \phi_{G'\ A} \circ F(\psi_A)\]
\[(F'\otimes \psi)_A \circ (\phi\otimes G)_A = F'(\psi_A) \circ \phi_{G\ A}\]
Naturality of $\phi$:
% https://q.uiver.app/#q=WzAsNCxbMCwwLCJGR0EiXSxbMSwwLCJGRydBIl0sWzEsMSwiRidHJ0EiXSxbMCwxLCJGJ0dBIl0sWzAsMSwiRihcXHBzaV9BKSJdLFsxLDIsIlxccGhpX3tHJ1xcIEF9Il0sWzAsMywiXFxwaGlfe0dcXCBBfSIsMl0sWzMsMiwiRicoXFxwc2lfQSkiLDJdXQ==
\[\begin{tikzcd}
	FGA & {FG'A} \\
	{F'GA} & {F'G'A}
	\arrow["{F(\psi_A)}", from=1-1, to=1-2]
	\arrow["{\phi_{G'\ A}}", from=1-2, to=2-2]
	\arrow["{\phi_{G\ A}}"', from=1-1, to=2-1]
	\arrow["{F'(\psi_A)}"', from=2-1, to=2-2]
\end{tikzcd}\]
\end{proof}


\begin{theorem}
    $[\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{C}]$ is a strict monoidal category.
\end{theorem}

\begin{example}
The monoids in $[\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{C}]$ are functors $F$ with natural transfomrations:
\[\mu: FF \rightarrow F\]
\[\eta: 1_{\mathcal{C}} \rightarrow F\]
that are associative and unital.

Associativity:
% https://q.uiver.app/#q=WzAsNCxbMCwwLCJGRkYiXSxbMSwwLCJGRiJdLFsxLDEsIkYiXSxbMCwxLCJGRiJdLFswLDEsIlxcbXUgXFxvdGltZXMgRiJdLFsxLDIsIlxcbXUiXSxbMCwzLCJGXFxvdGltZXMgXFxtdSIsMl0sWzMsMiwiXFxtdSIsMl1d
\[\begin{tikzcd}
	FFF & FF \\
	FF & F
	\arrow["{\mu \otimes F}", from=1-1, to=1-2]
	\arrow["\mu", from=1-2, to=2-2]
	\arrow["{F\otimes \mu}"', from=1-1, to=2-1]
	\arrow["\mu"', from=2-1, to=2-2]
\end{tikzcd}\]
Left Unit:
% https://q.uiver.app/#q=WzAsMyxbMCwwLCJGPTFfe1xcbWF0aGNhbHtDfX1cXGNpcmMgRiJdLFsxLDAsIkZGIl0sWzEsMSwiRiJdLFswLDEsIlxcZXRhXFxvdGltZXMgRiJdLFsxLDIsIlxcbXUiXSxbMCwyLCIxX3tcXG1hdGhjYWx7Q319IiwyXV0=
\[\begin{tikzcd}
	{F=1_{\mathcal{C}}\circ F} & FF \\
	& F
	\arrow["{\eta\otimes F}", from=1-1, to=1-2]
	\arrow["\mu", from=1-2, to=2-2]
	\arrow["{1_F}"', from=1-1, to=2-2]
\end{tikzcd}\]
Right unit:
% https://q.uiver.app/#q=WzAsMyxbMCwwLCJGPSBGIFxcY2lyYyAxX3tcXG1hdGhjYWx7Q319Il0sWzEsMCwiRkYiXSxbMSwxLCJGIl0sWzAsMSwiIEZcXG90aW1lc1xcZXRhIl0sWzEsMiwiXFxtdSJdLFswLDIsIjFfe0Z9IiwyXV0=
\[\begin{tikzcd}
	{F= F \circ 1_{\mathcal{C}}} & FF \\
	& F
	\arrow["{ F\otimes\eta}", from=1-1, to=1-2]
	\arrow["\mu", from=1-2, to=2-2]
	\arrow["{1_{F}}"', from=1-1, to=2-2]
\end{tikzcd}\]
    
\end{example}

\subsection{Monads}

\begin{definition}
    A monad is a monoid in $[\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{C}]$.
\end{definition}
\begin{note}
    Think of monads as some sort of inductive instruction.
    E.g.
    There's always a natural of of flattening lists of lists,
    or gluing trees of trees.
\end{note}

\begin{example}
\texttt{List} is a monad. $\mu_A: \texttt{List}^2\ A \rightarrow \texttt{List}$ is "flatten".
\[[[a_1^{(1)}, ..., a_{k_1}^{(1)}], [a_1^{(n)}, ..., a_{k_n}^{(n)}]] 
\mapsto [a_1^{(1)}, ..., a_{k_1}^{(1)}, ..., a_1^{(n)}, ..., a_{k_n}^{(n)}]\]
\[\eta_A : A \rightarrow \texttt{List}\ A\]
\[a\in A \mapsto [a]\]
Associativity:
% https://q.uiver.app/#
\[\begin{tikzcd}
	{\texttt{List}^3\ A} & {\texttt{List}^2\ A} \\
	{\texttt{List}^2\ A} & {\texttt{List}\ A}
	\arrow["{\texttt{List} \otimes \mu}", from=1-1, to=1-2]
	\arrow["\mu", from=1-2, to=2-2]
	\arrow["{\mu \otimes \texttt{List}}"', from=1-1, to=2-1]
	\arrow["\mu"', from=2-1, to=2-2]
\end{tikzcd}\]
Unit:
% https://q.uiver.app/#
\[\begin{tikzcd}
	{[a,b,c]} &&& {[[a],[b],[c]]} \\
	& {\texttt{List}\ A} & {\texttt{List}^2\ A} \\
	& {\texttt{List}^2\ A} & {\texttt{List}\ A} \\
	{[[a,b,c]]} &&& {[a,b,c]}
	\arrow["{\texttt{List}\otimes \eta}", from=2-2, to=2-3]
	\arrow["{1_A}"{description}, from=2-2, to=3-3]
	\arrow["\mu", from=2-3, to=3-3]
	\arrow[maps to, from=1-1, to=1-4]
	\arrow[maps to, from=1-4, to=4-4]
	\arrow["{\eta\otimes\texttt{List}}"', from=2-2, to=3-2]
	\arrow["\mu"', from=3-2, to=3-3]
	\arrow[maps to, from=1-1, to=4-1]
	\arrow[maps to, from=4-1, to=4-4]
\end{tikzcd}\]
\end{example}
